title: Grateful Dead Live at Onondaga War Memorial  on 1971-10-27
lineage: Dat (Sony R500) -> SEK'D Prodif Plus -> Samplitude Professional v8.01 -> FLAC
source: SBD -> Master Reel -> Cassette -> Dat (48k) D

ai_review.summary: Pristine soundboard capture of a classic 1971 set with a smoking Cumberland, Truckin', and an unforgettable Casey Jones opener.
ai_review.review: This recording delivers crystal‑clear Miller soundboard audio that lets the band’s 1971 energy shine through. Highlights include a blazing "Cumberland," tight "Truckin'"/"NFA/GDTRFB" medley, and a memorable opening with NRPS and Jerry on pedal steel, while Keith’s piano adds fresh texture. Overall the show is regarded as a high‑energy, quintessential early‑’71 performance.

ai_rating.rationale: The majority of reviews are 4–5 stars and praise both the performance and audio quality; only a few outliers rate low, so the weighted average reflects a strong show with excellent soundboard recording.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Clear, pristine Miller sbd tape with no reported dropouts or mix issues; reviewers note the audio sounds “pristine” and captures the band’s dynamics well.

standout_songs: Not Fade Away / Going Down The Road Feeling Bad
show_quality.setlist_flow: Typical early‑'71 two‑set structure with a strong first set opener and tight transitions; the second set stays focused without long jams but ends on a high note.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for expressive vocals (especially on "Comes a Time") and his pedal‑steel cameo with NRPS; fans note his tone and presence throughout the show.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith is highlighted as a welcome addition on piano, helping to solidify the new material and adding fresh texture to the set.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann’s drumming gets special mention with visual fireworks during "Casey Jones," underscoring his driving energy.
